evidenceAudit.scope: Adults who smoke or use other tobacco/nicotine (including shisha): asking, advising and treating dependence with behavioural support and medicines. Verified against the Saudi PHA Clinical Preventive Guideline 2023 (smoking cessation, grade A) and NICE NG209; doses and contraindications from FDA labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: NRT and cytisinicline doses not reproduced

pathophysiology.summary: Tobacco dependence is a chronic relapsing condition driven by nicotine. Tobacco smoke causes cancer, cardiovascular and respiratory disease; stopping at any age reduces risk.
keyMechanisms: Nicotine acts on brain nicotinic receptors → dopamine release → reinforcement and withdrawal on stopping.
Varenicline is a partial agonist that reduces craving and the reward of smoking.
Combined short- and long-acting NRT, or varenicline, with behavioural support are most effective (NICE NG209).

symptoms: Cigarettes, shisha, other tobacco or e-cigarette use; previous quit attempts; cravings and withdrawal.
physicalSigns: Exhaled carbon monoxide if available; signs of tobacco-related disease.
redFlags: Haemoptysis, weight loss, persistent cough — investigate

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Ask specifically — also delivers nicotine and smoke.

clinicalManagement.title: Ask and advise
actions: Record status; give clear advice to stop; offer support (PHA, NICE NG209).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat
actions: Offer behavioural support to everyone (NICE NG209).
Most effective with support: combination short- and long-acting NRT, or varenicline (NICE NG209). Cytisinicline and bupropion are other options; not under 18.
Varenicline: 0.5 mg once daily days 1–3, 0.5 mg twice daily days 4–7, then 1 mg twice daily for 12 weeks (label); set quit date or quit between days 8 and 35.
Prescribe before the quit date (NICE NG209).

clinicalManagement.title: Follow up
actions: Review progress, side effects and relapse; another 12 weeks of varenicline may be added for those who stopped (label).

learningObjectives: Identify tobacco use and treat dependence with support and medicines.
